Looking at the source data, a critical pattern emerges when examining words with final circumflex tone (̂):
- ḿbɔ́rɔ̂ → ńtʊ́bɔ́tʊ́rɔ̀ (rɔ̂ becomes rɔ̀)
- àwâ → àtʊ́wà (wâ becomes wà)  
- áyã̂ → átɪ̃́yã̀ (yã̂ becomes yã̀)
- mɔ̃́nɔ̃̂ → tʊ̃́mɔ̃́tʊ̃́nɔ̃̀ (nɔ̃̂ becomes nɔ̃̀)

The pattern is consistent: **any final syllable with circumflex tone changes to low tone in Agbirigba**. Since rʊ́tʊ̂ ends with circumflex tone, the final syllable must become tʊ̀. Candidate G correctly identifies and applies this tone-change rule (FIDELITY, CONFORMANCE). Candidates A, B, C, D, F all give tʊ̂tʊ̂ at the end, missing this required transformation. Candidate E ignores the pattern entirely. Candidate G's inference about tone changes, while imperfectly explained, yields the only answer consistent with the data's most robust pattern.
</why>
